subject: confusingly unlabeled output from predict function

messages.author: c2f90eaf0b3d2fff
messages.subject: confusingly unlabeled output from predict function
parts:
I ran this model using package unmarked: 

mod3 <- pcountOpen(~sites, ~1, ~sites, ~sites, adults, K=50, dynamics="constant", se=FALSE)

I have 20 sites, and 5 primary periods. I used the predict function to get estimates of survival, detection probabilities, and abundance but the output from that function has no labels on the rows to describe which site and which primary period are associated with each estimate. Is there some way to get predict() to show this information? 

my predict statement: 

preddata3 <-predict(mod3, type = "omega")

a few lines of the output: 

   Predicted SE lower upper
1  0.4880053 NA    NA    NA
2  0.4880053 NA    NA    NA
3  0.4880053 NA    NA    NA
4  0.4880053 NA    NA    NA
5  0.4880053 NA    NA    NA
.
.
.


Thanks!

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] confusingly unlabeled output from predict function
parts:
Hi Jillian,

If you don't specify the 'newdata' argument, the predictions are for each site in your data. If you want predictions for particular sites or particular covariate values, you need to provide a data.frame to the 'newdata' argument. And if you want the covariate values to appear with the predictions, you need to set the argument 'appendData' to TRUE.

Richard
